items.subject: An update to our Terms of Use
items.summary: Epidemic Sound is updating its terms of use for EU AI Act transparency rules, effective December 2, 2026.
items.body:
Changes relating to the EU AI Act.

We're updating our terms of use to reflect new transparency rules under the EU AI Act.

Content created or modified with our AI features, such as Adapt and Voices, will carry machine-readable markings, such as metadata and watermarks, that identify it as AI-generated or AI-modified. Please don't intentionally remove or tamper with these markings. Ordinary editing and exporting in your usual tools that incidentally changes metadata is fine.

The updated terms of use apply from 2 December 2026. If you don't use our AI features, this update doesn't affect how you use Epidemic Sound.

items.subject: Trust
items.summary: Elder Adamson shares a mission update from the ER with a torn shoulder, and reflects on trusting God's plan.
items.body:
Why do bad things happen to us? Why is there evil in this world? Why do we have to feel pain?

First off on a positive note HAPPY BIRTHDAY TO MY BOY MAX BARTON!!!

So bad news fans, I am writing this from the ER. I tore my shoulder. Not even the most tragic thing that happened this last week. BYU lost to Utah. Hence the preceding questions.

This has given me some time to reflect. Two main ideas have been on my mind lately: How do I trust in God's Plan? How do I better overcome adversity?

I know that the Book of Mormon provides answers to these questions. I do not know what will happen with my shoulder. It could be another torn labrum which means surgery. But I have full confidence that serving a mission is my commandment. Expect miracles, friends and family. Prayers would be much appreciated.

As far as overcoming adversity, I invite you all to listen to Jon Huntsman's BYU devotional: God Did Not Put Us Here to Fail.

Love you all,
Elder Adamson
